question: Solve \((2x-3)²=(x+1)²\). (Separate the two roots with a comma, writing them as integers or fractions in lowest terms.)
solution: Taking square roots on both sides gives \(2x-3=x+1\) or \(2x-3=-(x+1)\). The former gives \(x=4\); the latter gives \(3x=2\), so \(x=2/3\). Alternatively, move terms and factor using the difference of squares.

solutionMethods.explanation:
Subtract the squared expressions so that the difference-of-squares identity produces linear factors:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2x-3)^2-(x+1)^2&=0,\\
[(2x-3)-(x+1)][(2x-3)+(x+1)]&=0,\\
(x-4)(3x-2)&=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
A product is zero if and only if at least one factor is zero. Thus \(x-4=0\) or \(3x-2=0\), giving the two roots \(4,\,2/3\).
solutionMethods.label: Factor a difference of squares
